name: New Jersey

voter_file.who_may_get: Any voter, from the county clerk (printed registry lists) or the commissioner of registration (electronic list, at reproduction cost, max $375) (N.J.S.A. 19:31-18.1(a)-(b)).
voter_file.permitted_uses: Not as a basis for commercial or charitable solicitation (19:31-18.1(c)).

private_challenge.who: At the polls only: authorized challengers and district board members may challenge a person offering to vote; a challenge as an alien is handled by oath or naturalization certificate (N.J.S.A. 19:15-20). No pre-election written challenge by a private voter was found.
private_challenge.form_or_statute: N.J.S.A. 19:15-18.1 to 19:15-20. Not supported by JuryRoll.

county_board.name: New Jersey county election officials (Division of Elections)

ag.name: New Jersey Office of Attorney General

gates.basis: Jury records: status unknown (null), so counts only. Challenges exist only at the polls. Strict gates.

notes: UNVERIFIED: N.J. Court Rule 1:38-5(g). Secondary sources say it excludes juror qualification questionnaires from public access. The official text on njcourts.gov could not be fetched (bot wall), so jury_list.public and jury_list.statute stay null and the strict default applies.
Source note: election statutes were read from the Division of Elections statute pages on nj.gov.
A pending bill (A509, 2026 session) would match juror records against the voter system. It is not law and is not relied on.
official_pipeline is null: no enacted jury-to-election-official non-citizen statute was found.
